Can det3's calibration live with the beam-measured sharing kernel?

A screening test on the Saturday operating-point run: pin c1 and c2 to the H4 beam values, refit everything else inside a physical box, and see what it costs.

2026-08-17 · sat_det3 = mx17_det3_saturday_scan_6-27-26 / long_run_resist_490V_drift_1000V · 400-event ref-pinned calibration cache · nothing written to any bundle

Yes — and it costs nothing measurable. With c1 = 0.281 and c2 = 0.111 pinned to the H4 beam measurement, every remaining hyper lands inside its physical range, the sharing ladder is monotone, and against the frozen production bundle the cost is +1.7 % in ref-pinned χ2 and an angular-resolution change of −0.02 ± 0.06° (X) and +0.09 ± 0.07° (Y) — neither significant. In exchange the Y angle-compression slope goes 0.988 → 0.995, a 2.5σ improvement on the one metric RECONSTRUCTION_BASIS is about.

Two things fall out that matter more than the arm itself: the c2 > c1 inversion is not the C1_MIN floor's doing, and χ2 cannot make this decision — c1 varies 13× across the arms for under 5 % of χ2.

What was pinned, and where it comes from

The H4 beam measured det4's sharing kernel directly at normal incidence, which is the geometry that breaks the v ↔ sharing degeneracy a cosmic fit cannot (M70V_FLAT_ANALYSIS.md, run_56 flat, Y view, 625 V): c1 = 0.281, c2 = 0.111, τRC = 298 ns, invariant to 1–2 % over a 6 % gain step, with kY = c1,Y/c1,X = 1.12 (tilt-contaminated, indicative only).

That measurement has never been applied. wft/calibrate.py has a fixed= argument whose docstring names the H4 beam explicitly, and across all 90 bundle.json on the data disk provenance.fixed_hypers appears only in the det3 v-refits, pinning the cosmic hypers. Note the standing caveat: a kernel is per-detector and the SPS document is explicit it does not transfer, so the honest reading of what follows is "det3's data is compatible with the beam kernel", not "det3's kernel is 0.281/0.111".

The arms

Seven hyper sets, all ref-pinned on the same 180 training events with v pinned at 36.6 µm/ns, then scored on 220 held-out events. Each arm re-measures its own absolute-t0 table before being judged — the σ = 5 ns trigger prior was measured with lp2's τs = 145 ns, and reusing it penalises any arm that moves τs. χ2 is cold-started for every arm, because the optimiser's own warm-started number flatters a refit by ~20 %.

The recommended set

The kY is the part worth dwelling on. Only the amplitudes were pinned; kY was free over 0.3–6.0 and it landed at 1.29, next to the beam's own independently measured 1.12 — and nowhere near production's 2.88. The cosmic data chooses the beam's X/Y ratio when it is allowed to. Likewise τs = 79 ns against a measured ±1 peak shift of 54–61 ns, and σp0 falling from 0.409 to 0.254 mm — the extra 0.15 mm of "initial cloud" in the production bundle is the sharing it is not modelling.

The resolution penalty is not significant on either plane. The compression improvement is (2.5σ on Y for beam, 3.6σ for beamY). Note also that the production bundle is the only arm with a materially compressed Y slope — every refit, physical or not, fixes it.

The floor is not what inverts the ladder

This corrects an earlier reading. The obvious story — C1_MIN = 0.05 is a hard penalty wall, the optimiser parks on it, and the sharing it still needs spills into c2 — is only half right. The freeold arm settles it: seeded in the physical basin (c1 = 0.288) and turned loose with no floor at all, the fit slid to c1 = 0.022, kY = 3.18, c2/c1 = 2.76 — deeper into the inversion than production, and with the best χ2 of any arm.

So the ref-pinned cosmic χ2 on near-vertical tracks genuinely prefers "almost no sharing plus a wide cloud", from either starting basin. C1_MIN only decides where the slide stops — which is why every calib_bundle_lp* in the fleet sits at 0.050–0.115. The root cause is the v ↔ sharing degeneracy, and the floor is a brake on it, not its origin. Adding a c2 ≤ c1 ordering constraint would therefore bind, not merely tidy up.

χ2 cannot make this call

Across the seven arms c1 spans 0.022 to 0.281, a factor of 13, while held-out χ2 spans −3.4 % to +1.7 %. The arm with the best χ2 has the most unphysical kernel. This is the degeneracy quantified, and it is the same warning KERNEL_ARMS_2026-08-12.md §3 gives after two arms bought −23 % of χ2 with zero geometry gain.

The production bundle is internally inconsistent

Hold lp2's kernel fixed and scan the drift velocity alone:

v [µm/ns]   28      31      34     36.6     39      42      46
chi2      1.847e8 1.639e8 1.516e8 1.452e8 1.422e8 1.409e8 1.419e8
                                   ^bundle         ^minimum

χ2 wants v ≈ 42 µm/ns, 15 % above the 36.6 the bundle ships and uses everywhere; the shipped value costs +3.1 %. Pin the beam kernel instead and the freely fitted v comes back at 38.3, within 5 % of the bundle's own number. Too little modelled sharing has to be paid for with too fast a drift — which is exactly the failure mode an external kernel exists to prevent.

Follow-up: is the beam number generalizable, and how underconstrained are we?

Three questions came back, and all three turned out to be measurable rather than arguable.

1. The kernel is a board property — for four of the five chambers

The SPS campaign's real deliverable was not the number 0.281, it was a bench-portable, model-independent estimator (05_beam_kernel_xcheck.py): peak-aligned neighbour stacks on near-normal tracks, no bundle, no forward model. Run on every June calibration cache:

chamberplanen±1 / centre (pk) ±2 / centre±2 / ±1±1 area ±1 peak shift
det2X700.4010.0580.1440.399+28 ns
det3X940.3930.0420.1070.421+30 ns
det4X780.3400.0380.1120.354+37 ns
det7X390.3740.0330.0870.317+17 ns
det6X280.1280.0360.2840.132+20 ns
det2Y990.4110.1450.3530.559+86 ns
det3Y1240.4220.1210.2860.563+69 ns
det4Y1090.3620.0770.2120.510+45 ns
det7Y640.4190.1510.3610.613+67 ns
det6Y440.2690.1310.4880.439+122 ns

Across det2/3/4/7 the ±1 amplitude agrees to 6 % (X 0.377 ± 0.024, Y 0.403 ± 0.024) and the ±2/±1 ratio to ~20 % — every chamber monotone, and the Y ratio (0.303 ± 0.060) sitting on the beam's c2/c1 = 0.395. det6 is the exception and its X view is not in the family at all (0.128 against 0.34–0.40); it is also the gain-limited chamber with the smallest sample, so it is a flag, not yet a finding.

kY falls straight out, and it is not 2.88. Peak-ratio Y/X per chamber: det2 1.02, det3 1.07, det4 1.07, det7 1.12 — against the beam's independently measured 1.12 and the fitted 1.29. Production's 2.88 is not a measurement of anything.

But the area ratio Y/X is 1.34–1.93, and the peak shift is +28 ns on X against +67 ns on Y. So Y's copy is not stronger, it is slower — and a model with one shared delay can only represent "more area" by inflating the amplitude. That is what kY = 2.88 is: a timing difference booked as an amplitude.

Two limits on transferring the beam number even so. Between beam and bench on the same chamber (det4) there is a ~20 % gas offset in the stack-peak ratio (BEAM_CONSTRAINED_CALIB_2026-08-05.md §1) — more prompt diffusion in Ar/iso than in the cooled wet CF4 mix. And no per-chamber surface resistivity measurement exists: the only ρs on record is 2 MΩ/sq with a 1.42–2.56 band from T2b, and I could not establish that band as a chamber-to-chamber spread rather than one chamber's uncertainty. If it is chamber-to-chamber, the RC constant varies ±28 % and the delay with it.

2. Underconstrained, quantified: the χ2 determines v and almost nothing else

Numerical Hessian of the cold-start ref-pinned χ2 in log-parameter space, at the beam-pinned optimum, over all eight coordinates. Cost is the fractional χ2 rise for a 10 % coordinated move along each eigenvector:

modeΔχ2 per 10 % movemove needed for 1 % χ2dominant components
01.760 %7 %v
10.247 %20 %c1 −0.61, kY −0.58, σp0 −0.45
20.087 %34 %c2 +0.74, c1 −0.42, σs −0.37
30.067 %39 %τs +0.84, σs −0.37
40.047 %46 %σs +0.71, σp0 −0.41, kY +0.40
50.028 %60 %kY −0.62, c2 +0.61, c1 +0.41
60.011 %96 %Dp +0.97
7−0.009 %never — downhillσp0 −0.72, c1 +0.46, τs −0.37

Stiffest / softest positive eigenvalue = 162. Only v is stiff; a 1 % χ2 change costs a 7 % move in v but a 20–96 % move in every kernel/geometry combination, and mode 7 — the c1 ↔ σp0 trade — is flat to the resolution of this Hessian and slightly downhill. That is the escape route the free fits take, and it is why pinning c1 and c2 to the beam cost only 1.7 %.

So the diagnosis is not "too few data". It is that this objective is blind along exactly the directions the kernel lives in, while the model-independent estimators above measure those same directions to a few percent. The information is in the data; the χ2 is the wrong instrument to extract it with.

3. The delay: measurable at the SPS, not transferable into tau_s

The ±1 peak-time shift is the SPS's best-determined kernel observable — model-independent, drift-invariant across 700/450/275 V, and far more robust than c2 or τRC (which carry a ±30 % window systematic). The fleet table says it is per plane: +28 ± 7 ns on X, +67 ± 15 ns on Y. So two arms, on top of the beam amplitudes:

armτ effective X / Yχ2 held Δσθ XΔσθ Y Δslope XΔslope Y
beam (τ free)80 / 80 ns+1.7 % −0.023 (0.4σ)+0.089 (1.2σ) −0.0094 (1.9σ)+0.0074 (2.4σ)
+ τs = 58 ns pinned58 / 58 ns+1.3 % −0.029 (0.5σ)+0.114 (1.3σ) −0.0131 (2.6σ)+0.0015 (0.5σ)
+ per-plane τ (τY/τX free → 3.49) 30 / 105 ns+0.3 % −0.035 (0.6σ)+0.035 (0.5σ) −0.0234 (4.9σ)+0.0126 (3.7σ)

Two things happen at once. The per-plane arm confirms the mechanism emphatically — given the freedom, the fit walks τY/τX to 3.49 (measured ratio 2.4), reaches the best χ2 of any beam-pinned arm, and kills the Y compression outright (0.988 → 1.000, 3.7σ). And kY sits at 1.28–1.29 in all three arms, unmoved.

But X degrades monotonically as τs approaches the measured value: the X slope goes 1.004 (production, τ = 146 ns) → 0.994 (τ = 80) → 0.991 (τ = 58) → 0.980 (τ = 30, the measured X shift), the last at 4.9σ. The model wants a long X delay; the detector's X copy shifts by 28 ns. Those cannot both be right, and the resolution is that wft's tau_s is not the quantity the SPS measures: it translates a Gaussian-smeared template, while the observable is the peak of a dispersed RC copy. Substituting one for the other is the F19 lesson — RC constants are representation-dependent — now with a number on it.

Answer to "can the SPS constrain the delay too": it constrains the delay better than it constrains c2, and it says the delay is per-plane. It cannot constrain tau_s, because tau_s is a different quantity. Imposing it makes X worse, significantly. The amplitudes transfer; the time constant needs the kernel shape fixed first — a real per-plane RC response under the lp form, which is the post-MPGD26 project KERNEL_ARMS already nominated.

Is the measured kernel just transverse diffusion? No — the drift lever says so directly

Fair worry: a ±1 amplitude of 0.28–0.32 could in principle be the ionisation cloud simply being wide enough to straddle two 0.78 mm strips, with the resistive film contributing little. Two things settle it, and neither needs a model.

The measurement already separates them in TIME, not in space

kernel_fit_m70V.py does not fit one amplitude per neighbour. It fits two:

W_d(t) = alpha_d * W_0(t)  +  beta_d * (W_0 (*) K_tau^|d|)(t)
             prompt                    dispersed

α is charge that arrived with the central strip — diffusion, avalanche size, capacitive coupling. β is charge that arrived late, through the film's own sheet resistance. Diffused charge cannot be late; only the RC path can. So the split is done on arrival time, using the data's own central waveform as the basis — no shaper template, no drift model, no vdrift. For det4 Y at 625 V: α(±1) = 0.190, β(±1) = 0.281. c1 is β — the prompt part was already subtracted off.

And the drift lever confirms it independently

The SPS RAW arms hold gas, resist voltage and readout fixed and step only the drift field. σT ∝ 1/√E, so 243 → 95 V/cm inflates transverse diffusion by 1.6×. These are RAW — no zero suppression — with the ±1 neighbour detected 99.2–99.4 % of the time, so nothing is censored:

E [V/cm]n±1 peak±1 area ±2 peak±2 area±2/±1±1 shift
24339920.32630.41720.08130.09470.249+60 ns
15631720.32100.41990.08050.09950.251+60 ns
9523800.31480.40580.08110.09880.258+60 ns
spread over 2.6× in field1.5 %1.5 % 0.5 %2.2 %1.8 %0 ns

The scale of what a diffusion-borne signal would have done. On a 0.78 mm pitch, a Gaussian cloud giving ±1/centre = 0.32 needs σ ≈ 0.46 mm. Inflate that by 1.6× and the ratio goes to 0.60 — an 85 % change. Measured: 1.5 %. And ±2/±1 — the most diffusion-sensitive quantity there is, since a wider cloud reaches the second strip far faster than the first — moves by 1.8 %.

Transverse diffusion is not what these numbers are made of. c1 and c2 are the film.

Caveat, and it cuts one way. At 95 V/cm the drift ladder runs past the 3.84 µs window (RAW_RUN71_REANALYSIS §3), so the lowest-field arm preferentially keeps shallow, less-diffused charge — which biases against seeing a diffusion effect. The 243 → 156 V/cm step is barely truncated and still gives 1.6 %, and the ±2/±1 constancy is not explainable this way at all.

What the bench drift scan cannot do

det3's Saturday scan steps drift 100 → 1100 V at fixed resist — a far bigger lever (11× in field) whose calibration bundles were all built with the kernel pinned and only v refitted, so it had never been looked at. It does not work: the apparent ±1 peak ratio runs 0.19 → 0.44 (X) and 0.26 → 0.44 (Y) from low to high field, correlating with drift time at r = −0.97 — i.e. less apparent sharing when there is more diffusion, the wrong sign for the effect it would be measuring. The bench is zero-suppressed and its 1.92 µs window is shorter than the drift time below ~500 V, so at low field the slow shared copy is stretched below threshold and truncated away. This is TWOGAS_HEADON F3 — "cross-ZS comparisons of any tail quantity are invalid, full stop" — reproducing on the bench. Only RAW data can run this lever.

The angle lever: geometry is the contamination that actually matters

Diffusion is not the confound for a cosmic calibration — inclination is. wft is fitted on tracks to |tan θ| ~ 0.3, where the ionisation column itself walks up to 9 mm sideways across a 0.78 mm pitch. Same estimator, det3 at the operating point, binned in |tan|:

|tan θ|column walkX ±1X ±2 Y ±1Y ±2
0.00–0.050.7 mm0.3510.0370.4430.133
0.05–0.102.2 mm0.4060.0470.4210.114
0.10–0.163.7 mm0.4660.0860.4360.155
0.16–0.245.8 mm0.5150.1380.4940.190
0.24–0.409.2 mm0.5580.250——

X's ±1 grows linearly with the walk (0.024 per mm) and extrapolates to 0.355 at normal incidence — so 36 % of the top bin's apparent sharing is geometry. ±2 is worse: it grows 6.8× across the range, because an inclined column simply reaches the second strip. Y is much flatter (0.443 → 0.494), consistent with Y being film-dominated.

Two consequences. First, the normal-incidence intercepts (X 0.35, Y 0.44, and ±2/±1 = 0.11 / 0.30) reproduce both the fleet numbers and the SPS beam — the ±2 > ±1 inversion has no support at any angle. Second, this is plausibly why the cosmic χ2 slides: the model does have a geometry term (strip_fractions), but its width is set by σp0 and Dp, and σp0 is exactly the parameter that inflates to 0.41 mm to swallow the sharing. Geometry and sharing are being traded through the one knob that is supposed to separate them.

The lever that exists and has not been used

run63_rot25 and run62_rot25_ladder are det4 at 25.64° in the H4 beam, same gas and resist as the flat runs, with their own drift ladders. datasets.py and the timeline docs use them only for v(E). Nobody has fitted the kernel on them. A joint fit of the flat and 25.64° data — where geometry scales with tan θ and film sharing does not — is the clean simultaneous separation of geometry, diffusion and sharing, on a detector at known incidence with an external telescope. That is the measurement this whole thread has been circling, and the data for it is already on the staging disk.

What this is not

  • Not the bench harness. This is a screening test on the ref-pinned calibration cache with a reference-seeded free fit, so the absolute σθ is optimistic and the documented judges (within5, core σ, implied-v flatness, sNV) were not run. KERNEL_ARMS records arms that looked fine here and failed there.
  • Not a transfer claim. det4's kernel imposed on det3. The SPS document is explicit that kernels are per-chamber; the result is compatibility, not identity.
  • Near-vertical cosmics only (|tan θ| ≲ 0.3), one gas, one operating point.
  • Nothing was written. No bundle, no repo file, no re-reco, no fleet run.

One trap for whoever picks this up

13_full_recal.py caps sigma_s at 60 ns. That parameter is the dispersion of the shared copy — the same quantity the beam measures at ~300 ns — and the cap is binding for any beam-consistent kernel: the first pass of this test hit it exactly (59.91) and the arm looked ~0.05° worse than it is. The ceiling was inherited from an lp2-seeded fit that sat at 12 ns. Widen it before reusing that script.

Scripts: beam_pin_test.py (arms), beam_pin_fair.py (cold χ2 + per-arm t0 tables), beam_pin_v.py (v free), beam_pin_boot.py (paired bootstrap) — session scratchpad, not committed. Inputs: the existing calib_work/calib_cache.pkl and calib_bundle_lp2_t0p on the data disk. Beam numbers from sps_beam_test_26/analysis/M70V_FLAT_ANALYSIS.md.
